name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 68

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Give defence player a meal and get useful response

blocks.note: read with the words a meal later in the clue: to give a meal is to feed
a back is a defending player in football or rugby
completes the phrase begun by the first word, so it adds no letters of its own

explanation.surface: A coach treats a defender to dinner and gets some helpful comments in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ... a meal' is split around 'defence player', so the two halves of the wordplay interleave in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is information returned to someone about their performance, which is meant to help them improve.

clue.text: Player's warning about old city commotion

indicators.note: the golfer's call goes about, around, the ancient place

blocks.note: a golfer shouts this to warn others of a ball in flight
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A golfer's shout of alarm causes a stir in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the Sumerian city, is a crossword staple for 'old city'.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outbreak of public anger or excitement, a noisy commotion.

clue.text: Name the French girl who gets a man at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: elle is French for she
the end of the word man

explanation.surface: A French girl finally finds herself a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Elle, French for 'she', stands for a French girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Ass provides sound place for adaptable vicar

blocks.note: first meaning: the harsh cry of a donkey
second meaning: the parish in the song 'The Vicar of ...', whose vicar switched beliefs to keep his job

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Vicar of Bray' is an English song about a cleric who changed his religion with each monarch; Bray is a village in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's loud cry is called a bray, and Bray is the parish of the famously time-serving vicar.

clue.text: Can you start to take in chimney abuse?

indicators.note: the vessel word takes in, swallowing the next element inside
start points to the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: taken as written
lum is a Scots and northern word for a chimney
the opening letter of you

explanation.surface: An odd question about whether a sweep can tolerate insults about a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: Lum is a Scots and northern English word for a chimney, rarely met outside crosswords; 'Can' looks like the verb but is used as a word to be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is the making of false, damaging statements about someone, a form of verbal abuse or slander.

clue.text: Be defeated in court when secret place is revealed

indicators.note: one word sits in the abbreviation, so it is placed between its letters

blocks.note: to be defeated is to lose
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A litigant loses their case and some hidden matter comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small private room or cupboard, the classic hiding place for secrets and skeletons.

clue.text: Bird many conclude to be crazy

indicators.note: conclude points to the final letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: a loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver
the end of the word many

explanation.surface: Plenty of people decide some bird must be mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Loony is an informal word for mad or eccentric, so it is a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: Desire name for dramatic transport

blocks.note: surface reading: someone wants a name for something
setter's reading: a vehicle in a play called Desire, from Tennessee Williams's title

explanation.walkthrough: Tennessee Williams's play is 'A Streetcar Named Desire'; the clue reverses the title so Desire is the name of a theatrical vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title tells us the tram is named Desire, so the dramatic vehicle with that name is the streetcar.

clue.text: It's a tree chopped to make paper

indicators.note: something chopped up is broken into bits that can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree is felled and pulped to produce paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like the pulp product, but it means a written study.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work on a subject, the same sense as an academic paper.

clue.text: Soldiers inclined to be trustworthy

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
inclined or likely to do something

explanation.surface: A comment that troops tend to be dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a stock crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable can be depended upon, which is what being trustworthy means.

clue.text: Means to row in church, being rude

indicators.note: the rowing implement is placed in the church abbreviation, between its letters

blocks.note: Church of England, abbreviated
oars are the means by which a boat is rowed

explanation.surface: Having a row in church is a rude thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but here it is propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse language or behaviour is vulgar and crude, so rude is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pretentious nonsense British prince brought up

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means the name is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Talk of a British prince's upbringing is dismissed as pompous waffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Prince Henry, later Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is dismissive slang for empty, pompous or meaningless talk.

clue.text: Call for one to get around

blocks.note: first meaning: to telephone someone
second meaning: a circle or band, something to go round a finger or an arena

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asking someone to visit; the word is both a phone call and a circular band.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to telephone, and a ring is a circular band that encircles or goes around something.

clue.text: Money temp lost — about a pound — in work

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered from their places and must be rearranged
the rearranged letters go about, that is around, the weight abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A temporary worker has lost cash, around a pound, while on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound is not part of the shuffle: it is dropped into the rearranged letters afterwards, which is why 'about' is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment is paid work or a job, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Clever signal to get the last point in

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word that follows
the selected letter goes in, entering the signal word

blocks.note: a cue is a signal to begin
the end of the word point

explanation.surface: A shrewd signal allows the final point to be scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in its older sense means shrewd or sharp-witted, so it can mean clever.

clue.text: Get to know the room where criminal gets busy when one leaves

indicators.note: one is the numeral letter, and it departs from the word for a criminal

blocks.note: a study is a room for reading and work
a thief is a criminal
the Roman numeral for one
to get busy is to act, take action

explanation.surface: A burglar sets to work in a study once the occupant has left.
explanation.walkthrough: STUDY + THIEF without I + ACTS gives STUDY THE FACTS; 'the' belongs to the definition-free part, so 'room' alone gives STUDY.
explanation.definitionFit: To study the facts of a matter is to examine the information until you know and understand it.

clue.text: Fits ideas of revolution if enough is provided

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing someone whose needs are met

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the order, so these letters are turned into a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Revolutionary notions settle down once people have enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fits' could be outbursts and 'revolution' political, but together they just say shuffle these two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is satisfied when their wants or needs have been met, that is when enough has been supplied.

clue.text: Another one could be the making of them

definitions.text: Another one could be the making of them

blocks.clueFragment: Another one could be the making of them
blocks.note: surface reading: one more chance could make someone's fortune
setter's reading: add another one to one and the pair is made

explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points to a pair: one plus another one makes this number.
explanation.definitionFit: One and one more make a total of this number, so a second one creates the pair.

clue.text: Over-smart for a ride in a plane

blocks.note: first meaning: glib and flippant
second meaning: an informal word for a short pleasure flight

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a show-off taking a joyride; the answer is both an adjective and an old informal noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip means glibly flippant or cheeky, and a flip is a short trip in an aircraft.

clue.text: Proper disposal of what's left to gain favour

blocks.note: proper, suitable
a will disposes of the estate a person leaves

explanation.surface: Settling an estate fairly wins approval from relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left' sounds like leftovers, but it is an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is friendly feeling or kindly disposition toward someone, so it means favour.

clue.text: Where nation ends north of entire new state

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new state, that is a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geography note: a country's edge lies north of a whole newly founded state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' looks like the abbreviation N, but the whole word is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the border where one country stops, so a place at a nation's end is on the frontier.

clue.text: Reckon to have a price

blocks.note: first meaning: to estimate or assess
second meaning: a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Someone thinks everything has its cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to judge its worth, and a rate is a fixed charge or cost.

clue.text: Point to lots of money held by fools

blocks.note: north, a compass point
oodles means a great quantity

explanation.surface: Someone indicates the large fortune owned by some idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held by' looks like a container instruction, but it only joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an informal word for a silly person, so noodles are fools.

clue.text: Without accompaniment evil becomes glory when there's no alternative

indicators.note: no means the following item is absent from the word before it

blocks.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing
taken as written
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A moral that wrongdoing becomes glorious when there is no other choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' stands for the little word that offers a choice between two things, and 'no' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something singly is to do it alone or one at a time, unaccompanied by anyone else.

clue.text: Changing directions makes good sense

indicators.note: changing the word means altering the order of its letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that being willing to change course is the sensible thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is prudence or sound judgement in what one does or says, which is good sense.

clue.text: The man who has brought the dog back gets something frilly

indicators.note: the animal word comes back, written in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: The fellow who returned the dog is rewarded with a frilly item.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered or pleated frill of fabric used to trim clothing.

clue.text: Some of the nastiest stuff you could drink — surely not!

indicators.note: only some of the following word is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the second to the fifth of this word

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the idea of drinking the most foul liquid on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing 'surely not!' is a wink at the wine's cheap reputation rather than part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is something one could drink.

clue.text: Not moving yet

blocks.note: first meaning: motionless
second meaning: nevertheless, even so

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as 'not moving yet'; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means motionless as an adjective and nevertheless or even now as an adverb, the sense of yet.

clue.text: New turnover for reform

blocks.note: surface reading: a fresh business takeover or staff change
setter's reading: the idiom about mending one's ways, turning over a new page

explanation.walkthrough: To 'turn over a new leaf' is to reform one's behaviour; the clue squeezes the idiom into three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a reforming person turns over a fresh page of a book, and this is that page.

clue.text: Do take one in — being cold outside doesn't make sense

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a thing that does not make sense

indicators.note: the short word takes the numeral inside it, holding it between its letters
the word for cold sits outside, wrapping the rest

blocks.note: icy means very cold
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Taking someone in from the cold seems the sensible thing, so leaving them outside makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two wrappings, one inside the other: the numeral goes into the first word, and the result goes inside the word for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is extreme foolishness, behaviour or talk lacking in reason, which is what fails to make sense.

clue.text: Run away with money when starting to get short

indicators.note: the escape word is taken with the small coin inside it

blocks.note: running away is fleeing
c is the abbreviation for cent, a small coin

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with cash just as funds begin to run low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away with money' reads as one phrase for stealing, which fleecing also means; the definition is the shearing sense, a sheep starting to look cropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece a sheep is to shear off its wool, so a sheep being fleeced is starting to become short-coated.

clue.text: Deceives intake of commercial females

indicators.note: the verb word has an intake, so it swallows the next element inside

blocks.note: a liar deceives
a commercial is an ad

explanation.surface: Television advertising aimed at women is said to be misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is the polite plural for women, so it stands for females in general.

clue.text: Give complete employment in a way that helps

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: to employ something completely
second meaning: helpfully, to good purpose

explanation.surface: Advice to make full use of something so it is of benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it means put to complete use; as one word it is the adverb of useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Usefully is the adverb of useful, describing an action done helpfully or to good purpose.
